method.independence: No summary, reader answer, grade, previous reviewer report or parent chat history was read. The authorized ledger was read, including its recorded zero-addition passes.
method.coverage_standard: A fact in an answer key does not establish coverage unless substantive question wording elicits that fact. New questions must test a distinct explicit source rule, branch or consequential timing/exception, rather than a new number or mechanical combination.
method.preservation: No existing bank entry was edited or tightened. The two proposals below are additions only.

key_findings.finding: All 57 existing expected answers were checked against the assigned source; no material source contradiction requiring a key correction was found.
key_findings.detail: General answers about two production territories and home-base combat retreat are default rules; Q11 and Q33 separately elicit the Mill and Nordic Seaworthy exceptions. The keys' additional unasked details were not credited as coverage.

key_findings.finding: Default river/lake movement legality is not directly elicited.
key_findings.detail: Q27 asks faction Riverwalk/Swim exceptions and Q45 asks water geometry and ability-enabled entry. Neither requires stating the default prohibition that applies to all units before exceptions. Q05 asks unit count and transport, rather than terrain eligibility.

key_findings.finding: Enlisted recruit token permanence is only an unasked extra in Q12's key.
key_findings.detail: Q12 asks placement, one-time bonuses, ongoing-bonus linkage and resolution priority. It does not ask whether a token may subsequently be relocated. The source expressly makes it immovable, which prevents freeing a one-time bonus space by rearranging already enlisted recruits.

key_findings.finding: Diagram-dependent scoring keys agree with the source images.
key_findings.detail: Q39 tiers are 0-6, 7-12 and 13-18, paying 3/2/1, 4/3/2 and 5/4/3 per star/territory/resource pair. Q40-Q41 agree with all six pictured tile schedules and their duplicate, Mine, removed-encounter, river and longest-row qualifications.

proposed_additions.wording: Before any faction or mech ability provides an exception, may a character, mech or worker move across a river or onto a lake?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. By default, none of the three unit types may cross rivers or move onto lakes. An applicable special ability is required to override the relevant restriction.

source.passage: TYPES OF UNITS: all three unit types can move around the board, not over rivers or onto lakes by default.
RIVERS AND LAKES: By default, units may not move across rivers or onto lakes; some mech abilities break the rule.

proposed_additions.novelty: This is the source's categorical default movement restriction, distinct from the scope and destinations of particular exceptions. Q27 can be fully answered by listing each faction's Riverwalk and Nordic Swim permissions; Q45 can be fully answered by defining river borders and lake shorelines. A reader could answer both while incorrectly believing other units have unrestricted water movement. The proposal asks no new numerical example or combined ability scenario.

proposed_additions.wording: After placing an enlisted recruit on a Recruit One-Time Bonus space on your Faction Mat, may you move that recruit token later to free the space for another recruit?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. An enlisted recruit token remains on its chosen Faction Mat space permanently and cannot be moved. You cannot free an occupied one-time bonus space by relocating that token.

source.passage: ONE-TIME BONUS: place the recruit on any open Recruit One-Time Bonus space; the token remains there permanently and cannot be moved.

proposed_additions.novelty: This tests the explicit immobility restriction after initial placement. Q12's substantive wording asks where the recruit goes when enlisting, rather than whether it may later move; its key's word permanently is an unasked extra. The restriction has a gameplay consequence because rearrangement could reopen a one-time bonus space for reuse. It is a single source-defined placement/lifecycle restriction, analogous to the independently tested worker and structure permanence rules, not a recombination of unrelated mechanics.

rejected_candidates.candidate: May a player decline an ongoing recruit bonus, including one triggered by a neighbor?
rejected_candidates.reason: The source does use may gain. However, Q03 already tests optional action benefits and Q12 asks how the ongoing bonuses resolve. The neighbor example adds an application without a separately source-defined exception; insufficiently distinct to propose confidently.

rejected_candidates.candidate: May a third player join a combat with their own power or combat cards?
rejected_candidates.reason: The two participating players and their permitted spending are already elicited by Q07/Q13; Q38 covers the coin-only tangible alliance exchange. A third-party scenario largely restates those restrictions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Do unused combat cards earn coins at game end?
rejected_candidates.reason: Q20/Q39 cover the full scoring mechanism and categories. A standalone exclusion for a component outside those categories is reference padding rather than a new scoring branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Can a newly produced worker immediately increase the cost of the same Produce action?
rejected_candidates.reason: Q09 expressly asks whether new workers change the cost already paid.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Can a worker move first onto a mech and then be carried?
rejected_candidates.reason: Same transport-does-not-use-worker-movement rule elicited by Q05; reversing the example order is not a distinct rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: May a Mine owner use the Mine with a Factory Move while an opponent controls it?
rejected_candidates.reason: Combines Q11 owner-only persistent Mine ability and Q16 Factory movement rules; no new exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: May a sixth star stop an encounter or Factory card acquisition after combat?
rejected_candidates.reason: Q18/Q19/Q57 directly establish immediate mandatory sixth-star termination; a changed pending event is not a distinct rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Must spent resources be physically returned to the general supply?
rejected_candidates.reason: Covered consequence of paying resources; pile destination alone is low-impact handling/reference detail without a distinct game outcome.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Alternate tile layouts, popularity values, odd resource counts, worker counts or lake-battle cargo quantities
rejected_candidates.reason: Same source-defined branches already elicited by Q09/Q20/Q30/Q33/Q39-Q42/Q47; changed quantities are not additions.
Q03 elicits optional benefits; this is an example of the general rule, not a separate exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Additional shuffle procedures, combat-card value distribution, dial assembly, encounter reference numbers and achievement-sheet signatures
rejected_candidates.reason: Routine setup, component/reference or commemorative detail, rather than a missing substantive rule under the requested novelty threshold.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Delay of Game, sample scoring/quick-start recommendations, Automa, promo cards and expansion interactions

limitations: This is a coverage and source-alignment review of the supplied bank, not an evaluation of any summary or reader responses.
Detailed p26 own-turn objective timing controls over the abbreviated p2 quick-reference wording at any time.

The p25 Factory text describes the entire Move ending at an encounter/opponent, while p11 describes the moving unit stopping. Factory Move moves only one unit, so no distinct unresolved outcome requiring another question was identified.
The two proposed IDs are suggestions for the parent to assign; existing 57 entries must remain unchanged.
